name: What is the difference between open-cell and closed-cell spray foam?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between open-cell and closed-cell spray foam?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open-cell spray foam is a less dense, more flexible material with a spongy texture, allowing air to fill its open cells. It's effective for sound dampening and fills cavities well, but has a lower R-value per inch and is vapor-permeable. Closed-cell spray foam is much denser and more rigid, with its cells completely closed. It offers a higher R-value per inch, acts as a vapor barrier, and can add structural integrity. The choice depends on the application, climate, and desired R-value and moisture control.
acceptedAnswer.description: Open-cell foam is less dense, flexible, good for sound, with a lower R-value. Closed-cell foam is denser, rigid, provides higher R-value, and acts as a vapor barrier.
